texts: On day 605 of Year 2, a spring storm struck the harbor in the early evening.
Three fishing boats were at sea.
The three boats followed the lanterns of the Harbor Row.
The keepers of the Harbor Row refilled the mire-essence early.
The keepers of the Harbor Row shielded the lanterns against the wind.
The lanterns of the Harbor Row burned through the storm.
All three boats reached the harbor safely.
Joren Salt was on one of the three boats.
Joren Salt reached Meren Tallowhand's station before dawn.

q2_gaps: A bare temporal/frequency-relative adverb on a verb ("refilled the mire-essence early") — it is not a Manner adverb, not a day-part constant, not a deictic and not a calendar term, so it has no licensed slot; the instruction set names sequence/scope/degree adverbs as gap-worthy but never covers 'early/late' as a point-in-the-day qualifier.

A MODIFIED day-part in a time adjunct ("in the early evening") — day-parts are specified only as bare symbols (morning/afternoon/evening/night), with no rule for a modifier on one (fuse into a single constant, decompose as a compound kind, or drop the modifier).

A static position predicate over a definite/counted plural ("Three fishing boats were at sea") — the instruction set fixes that a copular predicate on a plural distributes by rule and that a counted plural with a distributive predicate keeps the group EVENT plus the rule, but never says whether a LocatedIn/position atom rides the group symbol, distributes per member, or both.
review.notes: Two role calls are borderline but licensed as written: Theme on "struck the harbor" (the does-the-object-change test is unclear, and the instruction set defaults unclear cases to Theme) and Patient on "refilled the mire-essence". Coreference, the group/rule split (group event + rule for the counted plurals, rule-only for the explicit universal "all three boats"), the partitive for "one of the three boats", and the entity-attached On/Against/Through prepositions all follow the doctrine.
